before: the path or course (plain)
after: a recurring way that can be invited to, cut off, or divinely guided
reason: The focus has ٱلسَّبِيلِ, and 29:29 says وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ before the focus says Satan turned them away from it. The repeated س ب ل forms in 29:12 and 29:69 widen this into a surah motif, though the usage remains within the ordinary path sense.

before: the recognized way or route (plain)
after: a route physically cut off and morally obstructed
reason: The phrase وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ in 29:29 gives the path a concrete obstruction image. Beside ٱلسَّبِيلِ and فَصَدَّهُمْ in 29:38, that earlier cutting makes Satan’s diversion sound like another way of blocking the route.

before: the path (plain)
after: the morally straight course named in the recurring prayer
reason: Fatiha 1:6 names ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ, a straight path, which directly calls the path branch beside ٱلسَّبِيلِ. The contrast sharpens because 29:38 says فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ, while the prayer repeatedly asks for the straight route.

before: the way (plain)
after: a way reached through guidance
reason: The imperative ٱهْدِنَا in Fatiha 1:6 explicitly asks to be guided to ٱلصِّرَٰطَ, so both the destination and the act of finding it are present. Against that prayer, عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ in the focus marks a course from which the people were turned.

before: people who travel the roads, including a traveler cut off from home
after: the traveler’s absent home made visible as ruins
reason: مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ names the people’s dwellings, which supplies the home-reference needed by the dictionary’s ابن السبيل traveler away from home. The verse presents ruined settlements rather than travelers, so this is a weak home-and-road echo.

before: the road and its users
after: travelers exposed when a road is cut off
reason: In 29:29 the words وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ explicitly put road users at risk by cutting the route. The same surah then says فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ in 29:38, so the traveler branch is activated by the concrete road-cutting phrase and carries into the focus obstruction.

before: a path or route (plain)
after: people being led along a way
reason: ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ in Fatiha 1:6 places people asking to be guided onto a route, directly activating the road-user image. The focus’s plural object in فَصَدَّهُمْ is likewise a group of people who have been moved away from ٱلسَّبِيلِ.

before: something hanging down, including a tail or rear end
after: a faint tail/end echo beside the word for sin
reason: The word بِذَنۢبِهِۦ in 29:40 means “by its sin,” while the related Arabic noun ذَنَب can mean a tail or rear end. That gives the downward-hanging branch a real but weak lexical foothold; the verse itself describes wrongdoing, not a tail.

before: lowering or releasing something from above
after: a punitive descent sent down
reason: The participle مُنزِلُونَ in 29:34 means that the punishment is being sent down, directly activating the branch of downward release. The focus names the dwellings as visible evidence after destruction, so this earlier descent gives the ruin its vertical force.

before: letting something fall from a height
after: a descent whose source is explicitly the sky
reason: The phrase مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ in 29:34 supplies the height from which the punishment comes, completing the branch’s above-to-below image. With مُنزِلُونَ in that same verse, the sky is not an arbitrary setting but the stated source of the descent.

before: a downward release from above
after: a possible vertical frame opened by the heavens
reason: ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ names the heavens, the upper region presupposed by a downward release. Nothing in 29:52 actually falls, so this is only a partial height cue.

before: rain falling between cloud and ground
after: rain’s skyward source suggested by the punishment from heaven
reason: ٱلسَّمَآءِ in 29:34 is the upper source from which the branch’s rain descends. The verse speaks of punishment rather than rain, so the sky supplies only one side of the image.

before: rain or a falling shower
after: a weather-like barrage sent upon a people
reason: أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِبًا describes a storm of stones sent upon one group, and حَاصِبًا gives the sending a falling-weather quality. It is not water, so the rain branch is an echo rather than the verse’s sense.

before: rain between heaven and earth
after: the upper half of a possible rain image
reason: ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ in 29:52 can call the sky side of the rain branch. The verse contains no rain or descent, leaving the branch only partly triggered.

before: rain as a descent from cloud toward ground
after: punishment falling from the sky in a rain-like pattern
reason: The concept path runs through descent and height: مُنْزِلُونَ and مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ meet in 29:34, while the rain branch describes water between sky and earth. That passage evokes falling precipitation, but its named substance is رِجْزًا, punishment, so the result stays a note.

before: rain falling from sky to ground
after: a vertical sky-to-earth span that can carry the rain image
reason: The bridge joins ٱلسَّمَآءِ in 29:34 to ٱلْأَرْضِ in 29:36, supplying both endpoints of the dictionary’s rain-between-heaven-and-ground image. In the surrounding destruction account, that span lets the rain branch resonate with punishment descending from above onto the land.

before: upper-lip or beard hair
after: a faint bodily-sensation echo beside the verb “perceive”
reason: The word يَشْعُرُونَ means “they perceive,” while the related Arabic root ش ع ر also names bodily hair. That sound-and-sense overlap offers a faint bodily cue for the hair branch, but 29:53 speaks of awareness and names no hair.

before: a bucket, especially one filled to its rim
after: a possible full-measure image beside each group’s sin
reason: بِذَنۢبِهِۦ names the sin for which each group is seized, and the related Arabic form ذَنُوب can name a full bucket. The punishment context permits a “full measure” echo, though the focus verse does not itself mention a vessel.

before: a bucket rim or vessel edge
after: a bucket image carried through the concept path to the word for sin
reason: This concept path moves from the bucket’s rim to a bucket part, then through the bucket concept to بِذَنۢبِهِۦ in 29:40. The shared bucket association can suggest a filled measure of guilt, but the last word means sin in its verse, so the link remains tentative.

before: a web-like film over the eye
after: a possible veiling or blocking echo
reason: فَصَدَّهُمْ means that they were turned away, which supplies a weak idea of obstruction beside the dictionary’s eye-covering disease. The focus names no eye, so the eye veil is only a note here.

before: an eye disease that forms a web-like veil and impairs sight
after: a web over sight set beside their claimed discernment
reason: مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ names people possessing or seeking clear perception, directly activating an eye disease that veils vision. The branch can therefore sound beside the paradox: they had sight or insight, yet Satan beautified their deeds and turned them from the path.

before: a web-like membrane over the eye
after: the spider-web image made explicit by the next ayah
reason: The branch describes the eye film as resembling a spider’s web, and 29:41 names ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ and its بيتًا. That explicit spider word calls the branch’s distinctive web image across the nearby ayah boundary.

before: an eye condition linked to harm by the evil eye
after: a faint eye-harm echo beside “themselves”
reason: أَنفُسَهُمْ in 29:40 supplies the word نفوس/أنفس that can enter the idiom for harm through the evil eye. Here the groups harm themselves by wrongdoing, so the ocular branch is only weakly called.

before: an eye veil that impairs sight
after: an eye condition heard beside an explicit command to look
reason: The command فَٱنظُرُوا۟ in 29:20 explicitly calls for looking, a direct visual trigger for the eye branch. It also gives a useful surah contrast with مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ in the focus, whose possessors of discernment were nevertheless diverted.

before: a red-veined web over the eye
after: an eye-image carried through the concept chain to another sight-loss branch
reason: The concept path runs from the eye disease through the eye category to the listed blind-eye branch attached to يَٰقَوْمِ in 29:36. The ordinary word means “my people,” so the eye image is a deliberately remote dictionary echo rather than a reading of that address.

before: a web-like eye disease that obscures sight
after: an ocular-image cluster beside the focus’s language of insight
reason: مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ puts sight and discernment in the focus, while ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ in Fatiha 1:7 has a dictionary branch for swelling around the eye. That second eye condition activates the focus’s eye-veil branch, letting the prayer’s ordinary “those under wrath” carry a brief ocular resonance.

before: a web-like illness that clouds vision
after: a weak uprightness-and-sight contrast beside the straight path
reason: ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ means straight or upright, which partially meets the listed standing-eye branch associated with loss of sight. The Fatiha phrase has no eye word, so it gives only a weak contrast with the focus’s مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ.

before: a web over the eye
after: a faint eye-delight counterimage beside a gift of favor
reason: أَنْعَمْتَ in Fatiha 1:7 can call the idiom that treats someone as the eye’s delight or comfort, supplying a positive eye image beside the focus’s sight language. The prayer says “You favored,” not “eye,” so the disease branch receives only a light counterimage.

branch: س ب ل B010 + 29:41 spider-web image
before: people with insight (plain)
after: discernment obscured as though a spider web covered the eye
reason: ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ and بَيْتًا in 29:41 supply the actual spider and its web-built dwelling, matching the dictionary’s web-like eye veil. Joined to مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ and the focus’s account of Satan beautifying deeds, the image makes their claimed insight sound clouded and ensnared.
